chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Yasir al-Khadim, who said:

The boys ate a fruit one day and did not scrutinize it, and threw it away. So Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to them: 'Glory be to Allah! If you are needless, so there are people who are not needless. Feed the ones who are needy to it'.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu Al-Hasan (Imam al-Reza or Imam al-Sadiq depending on context, here referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic teaching on food waste and sharing with the needy based on the behavior of the boys?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) uses this everyday incident to teach the principle of *Iqtisad* (moderation) and *Shukr* (gratitude), highlighting that waste (*Israf*) is not just about quantity but about ignoring the needs of others. This narration is frequently cited in Shia jurisprudence to establish the virtue of sharing surplus food with the poor, linking personal consumption habits to social responsibility.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Nuh Bin Shuayb, from Yasseer Al Khaddam who said,

‘The boys ate a fruit one day and did not scrutinize it, and threw it away. So Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said to them: ‘Glory be to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! If you are needless, so there are people who are not needless. Feed the ones who are needy to it’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Nuh ibn Shu’ayb from Yasir al-Khadim who has said the following: “

One day boys ate fruit but they did not eat them all and threw them away. Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, said to them, ’Allah is free of all defects, if you did not need them, there are people who need them. You must feed those who are needy.’”
